notation_and_syntax.notes: Failure-to-cached and failure-to-retry transitions are distinct; expected work is explicitly a screening model rather than a latency theorem.

evidence: Reproduced the exact five-line Python trace and confirmed one catalog build and two retry attempts.
Recomputed Exercise 3: 0.05 times 800 ms is 40 ms; 400 times 2 microseconds is 0.8 ms when used and 0.04 ms population-weighted; simplified total is 40.04 ms.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Cold-tail latency, concurrency, memory, failure, and fleet behavior are explicitly excluded from the arithmetic.

Checked publication and one-active-attempt predicates under stated synchronization assumptions.
Checked generation routing, holder pinning, and retire-after-zero-holders argument.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The sequential implementation intentionally does not satisfy the chapter's concurrent protocol without an external synchronization primitive.

evidence: Reviewed unused, simultaneous first use, duplicate attempt, partial publication, recursion/self-await, permanent/transient/caller-specific failure, failure poisoning, retry storm, waiter timeout, cancellation race, shutdown during initialization, and post-close access.
Reviewed ORM session closure/N+1, fleet warm-up stampede, invalidation under readers, credential rotation, essential readiness, autonomous-vehicle calibration, and radiation-therapy calibration.

evidence: Checked complete publication, one active attempt when claimed, recursion policy, classified failure/backoff/deadlines, waiter cancellation ownership, readiness alignment, coherent generations, and shutdown ownership.
invariant_checking.notes: The mechanisms, examples, alternatives, failures, exercises, and answers preserve these invariants and label exceptions.

Reviewed generation closure against unpublish-before-zero-holders assumptions.

proof_review.notes: Constructor self-leakage, arbitrary implementations, language memory models, liveness, and real resource lifecycle are expressly outside the proof.

evidence: Audited at-most-one, exactly-once, happens-before, safe, prove, proof sketch, healthy, ready, faster, retry, cancellation, and conclusion language.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Runtime primitives are described by their own documented guarantees, and proposed production/high-stakes evidence is not claimed as completed.

evidence: Exact sequential deferral, identity, build-count, retry-value, and attempt-count output reproduced.
Concurrency, timing, ORM, fleet, credential, vehicle, and radiation evidence remain future requirements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No performance improvement, production readiness, external practitioner, academic, clinical, or safety review is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter treats lazy initialization as a demand-time lifecycle state machine and distinguishes once, single-flight, retry, memoization, invalidation, and warming semantics.

practitioner_review.notes: The guidance covers explicit demand APIs, language primitives, readiness, fleet stampedes, ORM behavior, generation reload, metrics, root-owned shutdown, and service-budget-aware cancellation.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter progresses from a compact state model through concurrency and operations to a runnable trace, ten cross-domain examples, and five exercises spanning formal traces, async design, arithmetic, reload, and safety critique.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
